claims.detail: box-sizing:border-box does not shrink a replaced element whose width is auto, so the content box stays 560 (CSS-rule reasoning, not browser-measured). Parent is a column flexbox with align-items:center, so no stretch; if the centre grid column is narrower than 562px (viewport below roughly 1222px) the canvas overflows rather than scales. The background #05080c is never visible once a frame is drawn (drawMap fills the full canvas first, :740/:743). On a HiDPI display the 560px bitmap is upsampled by the browser (blur on 9px text / 1-2px strokes) because cv.width is never multiplied by devicePixelRatio. #timelinecard is 560px border-box (:535) vs the canvas's 562 outer - a pre-existing 2px mismatch. claims.statement: Berths are handed out per depot in order of DESCENDING distance from the nearest grid edge (tie-break x then y): UAV a gets ranked[a], firefighter i gets ranked[n_uavs+i]. Ring sizes 1/3/5/7/9 for edge distance 4/3/2/1/0, so the 9-cell OUTER ring (indices 16..24) is never a berth for any total unit count <= 16.
claims.detail: OUTER RING (edge distance 0): NW = (0,45),(0,46),(0,47),(0,48),(0,49),(1,49),(2,49),(3,49),(4,49) = the L along the canvas LEFT column (x 0..11.2px) and TOP row (y 0..11.2px). SE = (45,0),(46,0),(47,0),(48,0),(49,0),(49,1),(49,2),(49,3),(49,4) = the L along the canvas BOTTOM row (y 548.8..560) and RIGHT column (x 548.8..560). Units cluster at the INNER corner of each block (NW: screen bottom-right of the block; SE: screen top-left). Built-in scenarios (serve_dashboard.py:38-41) total 6/5/8/6 units -> highest index 7, so indices 8..24 = (4,47)/(47,4) + the whole d1 ring + the whole d0 ring (17 cells per depot) are never berths in any preset. Occupancy caveats: (a) firefighters and trackers always home at depot 0 = NW (wildfire_model.py:713-715, :769-773); only searchers can home at SE, and with ONE searcher (every preset: serve_dashboard.py:647 `firetrackers.value=Math.max(0,n-1);victimsearchers.value=1`) `_crosswind_band` returns None (local_adaptation_generator.py:372-373 `if n <= 1 ... return None`; wildfire_model.py:749-753 `continue`), so the SE depot starts EMPTY and only receives returning UAVs. With the spinners maxed (8 FT + 8 VS + 8 FF) UAVs take indices 0..15 (through the d1 ring) and the 8 firefighters take indices 16..23 on the NW outer ring. extra_findings: The depot violet is nearly invisible by luminance on the ground it actually sits on. Computed WCAG contrast of #770099 vs raw ground: veg #124b05 1.10, canvas base #1c630b 1.26, veg #459f30 2.79, veg idx0 #414141 1.09, burnt #2b2b2b 1.51, scorched #895e00 1.63, spared #2f4a1a 1.06, smoke #ababab 4.07, fire #fe5501 2.90, prob-white 9.36, prob-black 2.24. Against its own 0.22-alpha tint it is lower still (e.g. 1.01 on #1c630b, 1.49 on burnt). Every value except lightest-veg/yellow-fire/smoke/white is under the 3:1 the file itself uses as its bar (serve_dashboard.py:776-789). The file already contains the fix idiom - twoTone(): 3px #000 casing + 1px #FFF core with half-pixel snap (:790-795) - defined AFTER the depot block, so a marker that wants it must either move below :795 or inline its own casing.

UAV FOV frames overdraw the depot outline on the map-edge sides. The FOV block is clamped to the grid (:807-810), so for any UAV within 8 cells of an edge the frame's L/T snaps to 0.5px and its 3px black + 1px white stroke covers px -1..2 - exactly the depot stroke's 0..2px band. At spawn every unit sits in the NW depot (x<=4, y>=45), so the NW outline's top and left sides are hidden under FOV casing from frame 0; the FOV rect spans x 0..145.6px, i.e. the whole 56px depot edge. Computed from the code, not rendered. Anything drawn in the depot's current z-slot on the outer L is likewise under the FOV casing.

The two surfaces disagree on z-order: dashboard depot is UNDER all units and overlays; mesa depot (Layer 2) is OVER UAVs and UAV FOV bars (Layer 1) and under victims/firefighters (Layer 3). The mesa comment at Canvas_Grid_Visualization.py:136-137 describes layer 2 as below 'the unit markers (UAV/PathMarker at 1, ...)', which is numerically wrong for UAVs. Layer must stay an integer (:137-141; CanvasModule.js:63 for-in ordering). Mesa hover tooltips only work for the last-drawn layer (GridDraw.js:60,:128 re-init the lookup table and listeners per layer), so a depot tooltip on layer 2 would never show.

Both surfaces place NW at screen top-left and SE at bottom-right (dashboard y-flip serve_dashboard.py:763 `(H-d.y-d.size)*cs`; mesa GridDraw.js:72). The dashboard flips with H and scales x by W while the model has x on HEIGHT and y on WIDTH - recorded as inert at 50x50 in the comment at :756-761; a marker should reuse the same dx/dy expressions rather than re-derive them.

cs = 11.2 is non-integer: 80% of cell edges are off integer pixels (comment :787-789). The depot rect happens to land on integers (0, 56, 504, 560) because 5*11.2 = 56 and 45*11.2 = 504, so a marker aligned to depot corners is crisp, but anything aligned to interior cell boundaries (11.2, 22.4, 33.6, 44.8) is not, and needs the Math.round(v)+0.5 snap idiom.

WIND default asymmetry affects which depot burns behind the marker: common_fixed_variables.py:36 `WIND_DIRECTION = 'west'` (reaches `python main.py --mesa`), while the dashboard form defaults to east (serve_dashboard.py:567 first option). Per common_fixed_variables.py:237-248 NW is upwind of east/south and SE is downwind, so on default dashboard runs SE is the depot whose background turns fire/smoke/burnt; under the mesa default west it is NW.
Legend is unconditional: the 'base station' chip is shown even when BASE_STATION_MODE=0 yields depots=[] and nothing is drawn (setLegend at :721-723 never consults the frame).
